authTierRationale: The only credentials model (OAuthCredentials) makes access_token, client_id and client_secret all required, so standalone use requires the customer to register their own Meta app, add the Marketing API product, grant ads_management/ads_read/read_insights/business_management, and generate a token — T2_BYO_APP. It is not T3: no refresh token is collected and no refresh grant exists anywhere in the connector or its OAuth2Spec (accessTokenResponseMap maps only /access_token), so token longevity is entirely the user's problem. Estuary's control plane can run the authorization_code flow on the user's behalf (spec.py sets x-oauth2-provider: facebook and __main__.py supplies flow.OAuth2Spec with Facebook's v23.0 dialog/token URLs), which makes it feel T1 inside Estuary's UI — but the client_id/client_secret fields are still declared required in the config schema, so the standalone tier is T2_BYO_APP.

unionMisfits.description: This is the LEGACY facebook-marketing connector: it does not issue HTTP itself. Every read goes through the vendor `facebook_business` SDK (AdAccount.get_ads / get_ad_sets / get_campaigns / get_ad_creatives / get_custom_conversions / get_ad_images / get_ad_videos / get_activities / get_insights), which builds the Graph API URL internally. No literal endpoint path string exists in the connector source, so the `path` values here are recorded as `sdk:<method call>` rather than a URL, and the Graph edge names are deliberately NOT reconstructed.

proposedShape.note: transport is HTTP but the URL is owned by the SDK

unionMisfits.description: The insights streams are an async-report job, not a request/response read. Per date slice (time_increment days, default 1, per ad account) the connector POSTs get_insights(is_async=True) to create an AdReportRun, then polls async_status/async_percent_completion (batched, up to 50 status checks per batch, 30s between sweeps, 1h per-job timeout, max 20 attempts), and only then GETs the report result with limit=100. Concurrency is governed by the x-fb-ads-insights-throttle response header: no new jobs are started while min(per_account, per_application) > 70, and at most 100 jobs are in flight. A job that fails twice is split into per-campaign, then per-adset, then per-ad sub-jobs.

proposedShape.onFailure: split job account -> campaign -> adset -> ad

unionMisfits.description: The entity streams do not send a scalar `since`-style query param. They send Graph's structured `filtering` parameter: a JSON array of {field, operator, value} objects, where field is `<entity_prefix>.updated_time`, operator is GREATER_THAN and value is a unix-seconds integer. `include_deleted` merges a second clause on `<entity_prefix>.delivery_info` with operator IN. The `{param, format}` shape cannot express a filter-object path plus operator.

Images and Videos are 'reversed incremental': the Graph API returns them sorted descending by updated_time and accepts no server-side cursor filter (the code comments that filtering stopped working for videos on 2023-01-13). Incrementality is implemented purely client-side — the connector walks the descending page stream and BREAKS as soon as a record's updated_time is older than the stored bookmark. So the wire request is identical between backfill and incremental legs; only the client-side stop condition differs. Images additionally drop deleted records in code rather than via a filter.

Neither 'static' nor 'discovered' fits cleanly. 16 streams are a fixed shipped list; additional AdsInsights streams are minted from the ENDPOINT CONFIG (`custom_insights` array), not from the customer's remote schema. Recorded as 'mixed' with the custom-insight stream as an archetype named custom<Name> (snake-cased, so a custom insight named `ads_insights_publisher_platform` becomes the stream `customads_insights_publisher_platform`).
No schedule of any kind is expressed in the connector or in the estuary-cdk airbyte shim. Cadence is imposed entirely by the Flow runtime outside this code.

The base URL never appears in connector source; it is a constant inside the facebook_business SDK. The only in-repo corroboration that the host is graph.facebook.com is the OAuth accessTokenUrlTemplate. The version segment IS set by connector code (api_version="v23.0").

abstained.transports[0].spec.baseUrl.kind=constant: The literal host is never written in connector source — facebook_business owns it. Recorded as a template with only the version segment attributable to connector code.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No headers are set by the connector; the SDK builds them.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.path (literal Graph edg: The connector calls vendor SDK methods (get_ads, get_ad_sets, get_insights, ...); no URL path string exists in the source. Reconstructing edge names would be invention, so `sdk:<method>` is recorded instead.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.httpMethod: Not visible in connector code — the SDK chooses the verb. GET is asserted only for list reads because the patched Cursor issues self._api.call("GET", ...); POST for insights-job creation is inferred from it being a job-creation call and is NOT confirmed in-repo.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.recordsPath: "data" is inferred from the patched Cursor consuming response["paging"] alongside build_objects_from_response(response); the records key itself is read inside the SDK, not in connector code.
abstained.streams[].pull.backfill for ads_insights: There is no distinct backfill leg: the same async-job mechanism sweeps date intervals from _get_start_date() forward, so only `incremental` is populated.
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule / streams[].sc: No interval, cron, or duration literal exists anywhere in this connector or in the airbyte shim; cadence is set by the Flow runtime.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is poll and nothing is created server-side except transient AdReportRun report jobs, which the connector abandons rather than deletes; no lease/slot/consumer-group semantics apply.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: The connector emits records with keys and never emits deletes or tombstones; "merge" reflects Flow's keyed-collection reduction rather than an explicit connector declaration. Deleted objects appear as normal records only when include_deleted is set.
abstained.streams[ads_insights*].primaryKey orderi: Two sources disagree — see the FLAG in unionMisfits/notes. The committed acmeCo/flow.yaml keys (date_start, account_id, level_id, *breakdowns) were used; the current AdsInsights.primary_key property returns sorted(...) which would order them differently, and source.py passes yet another value (source_defined_primary_key=["id"]) for ads_insights_age_and_gender and ads_insights_action_type.
abstained.streams[].pull.*.params.fields: Field lists are derived at runtime from the shipped JSON schemas (hundreds of properties); enumerated only descriptively.
